notes: 'Integer-5 shall be greater than integer-4' - SR5 one general format over, and a separate row because the table's FORMAT column is re-derived from the standard's own bare FORMAT 1 / FORMAT 2 / FORMAT 3 division lines (RecordClauseRuleDriftTests.EveryRow_IsScreenedOnTheFormatTheStandardPrintsItUnder). Format 3 deliberately gets NO SR4-analogue: 13.18.43.4 GR18 says the size of each record 'is completely defined in the record description entry', so the standard states no rule bounding the descriptions by integer-4 and integer-5, and the negative golden asserts the record draws nothing while the clause is reported. The positive witnesses the boundary where SR9 must not fire (RECORD CONTAINS 4 TO 12 BYTES). The rule is ISO/IEC 1989:2002's (13.16.41.2 SR8): the 1985 text prints no ordering rule for Format 3 (its GR14 makes the two integers the smallest and largest record size, equal for a file of one size), so RecordClauseRules carries it Since 2002 and --std 85 accepts RECORD CONTAINS 5 TO 5 (kb/Work PB5196).
